explanation.text: The 26th Amendment to the United States Constitution, ratified in July 1971, lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.
The amendment concerning congressional pay was ratified in 1992 and became the 27th Amendment, not the 26th.
The Archivist of the United States certified the ratification of the congressional pay amendment on May 18, 1992.
Congress confirmed the certification of the congressional pay amendment as the 27th Amendment on May 20, 1992.

excerpts.text: ﻿Ratified in July 1971, the 26th Amendment to the United States Constitution lowered the voting age of U.S. citizens from 21 to 18 years old.

On July 5th, 1971, in a [ceremony in the White House East Room](https://youtu.be/_Fp0RZme39A), in front of the 500-member choral group Young Americans in Concert, President Richard Nixon signed the certified amendment along with three [selected 18-year-olds](https://www.jacksonsun.com/story/news/local/2018/11/06/meet-woman-who-signed-amendment-allowing-18-year-olds-vote/1905213002/) signing as witnesses.
